detail.problem: All four signs are present and give a probable Dehydration diagnosis; BP < 90/60 is split into SBP < 90 or DBP < 60 as the gold standard does. One concept quibble: 'Thirst due to water deprivation' is narrower than the page's 'thirst'; its parent 'Thirst finding' (finding) exists and matches the page's wording. Descendant matching means the rule would still fire on either, so the effect is confined to what the check_for asks the worker to record.

parts_missing: BP < 90/60 encoded as two independent ORed thresholds (SBP<90 OR DBP<60) -- reasonable reading
detail.problem: Footnote 2 defines dehydration likely by thirst, dry mouth, poor turgor, BP < 90/60: encoded as a probable rule with those OR criteria. Concern: 'Thirst due to water deprivation' is a narrower concept than 'thirst' (should be plain Thirst); 'Xerostomia' ok; 'Decreased skin turgor' ok. The rule is also gated on cardiac arrest, which is not in the footnote but fits the context. Also BP is unmeasurable in an arrest, so the BP criteria are of little practical use.

Footnote 2 'Thirst, dry mouth, poor skin turgor, BP < 90/60, dehydration likely' is encoded as a probable dehydration rule, but (1) any single item suffices via a flat OR, including a single isolated BP component; 'BP < 90/60' is split into systolic < 90 OR diastolic < 60, so a diastolic of 58 alone (or any low pressure recorded during an arrest, where BP is near-universally low/unrecordable) makes dehydration probable. The footnote list reads more naturally as a cluster, not any-one-of; at minimum BP should be one item. (2) 'Thirst' is encoded as 'Thirst due to water deprivation', which presupposes the cause and is a sibling of 'Increased thirst' under 'Thirst finding'; a recorded 'Increased thirst' would not match. Closer: 'Increased thirst' (or 'Thirst finding'). (3) The BP measurements are not checked for, but are routine vitals, so the test passes. Footnote 1 (adrenaline = epinephrine) is a note.

The same two findings are the due_to of the check_for task and the and-gate of both probable rules, so everything on the page hangs on them being recordable.

The page's discriminating finding, the heart rhythm (VF / pVT / asystole / PEA), appears nowhere.
